lean.statement:
∀
  {X : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} X] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} X}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u_1} μ] {Γ : (X → ℝ) → X → ℝ} {admissible : (X → ℝ) → Prop} {C l u : ℝ}
  {B : X → ℝ},
  LE.le.{0} 0 C →
    AEMeasurable.{u_1, 0} B μ →
      (∀ᵐ (x : X) ∂μ, LE.le.{0} l (B x)) →
        (∀ᵐ (x : X) ∂μ, LE.le.{0} (B x) u) →
          AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.BoundedPerturbation.EnergyLogSobolev.{u_1} μ Γ
              admissible C →
            AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.BoundedPerturbation.EnergyLogSobolev.{u_1}
              (MeasureTheory.Measure.tilted.{u_1} μ B) Γ admissible
              (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} C (Real.exp (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} u l)))
approved_definition_context: Measure comparison is comparison on all measurable sets. ENNReal.ofReal takes the nonnegative part into the nonnegative extended reals; scalar multiplication of a measure scales its mass. Integrable means genuine Bochner integrability, and ≤ᵐ[m] means almost-everywhere comparison under m.

For any measure m and real function h, entropy m h denotes (∫ x, h x * Real.log (h x) ∂m) - (∫ x, h x ∂m) * Real.log (∫ x, h x ∂m). These are real Bochner integrals; Real.log 0 = 0. This is not an extended-real entropy.

EnergyLogSobolev m G D c is the predicate: for every real function f, D f, Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2) m, Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2)) m, Integrable (G f) m, and 0 ≤ᵐ[m] G f imply entropy m (fun x => (f x)^2) ≤ 2*c*∫ x, G f x ∂m. D is a fixed arbitrary test-function predicate and G is a fixed energy-density map. The predicate does not assert that all D-tests have the displayed integrability.

The tilted law m.tilted B is m.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (B x) / ∫ y, Real.exp (B y) ∂m)). Its normalization is meaningful when the exponential is integrable; this is not a separate hypothesis in the displayed theorem.
